title: Peter Pan and Never Land.
lines: In a big house in London lives a girl.
Her name is Wendy.
She has two little brothers.
John, who wears glasses and a top hat, and Michael, the smallest, who always holds his teddy bear.
And they have a dog as their nanny.
A big, gentle dog called Nana.
Woof!
Every evening Wendy tells her brothers stories.
Exciting stories about pirates and about a boy who never wants to grow up.
That boy's name is Peter Pan.
But one night, when everyone was asleep, something happened.
The window opened.
Creeak.
And a boy flew in.
He wore a green suit and a green pointy hat with a red feather.
It was Peter Pan!
The real Peter Pan!
And with him was a little light that zoomed around.
Ping, ping, ping!
It was a fairy.
A tiny girl with little wings, who glowed like a little star.
Her name was Tinker Bell.
Peter Pan was looking for his shadow.
He had lost it!
He walked around, and his shadow ran away from him.
Hee hee hee!
Wendy woke up.
She sewed the shadow back onto his feet.
Come with me to Never Land, said Peter.
There you never grow up.
There it's always a party!
But how do we get there?
asked Wendy.
We fly, of course!
said Peter.
But Wendy and her brothers couldn't fly.
Then Peter picked up Tinker Bell and shook her gently.
Ping, ping, ping!
Glittering golden dust swirled off her.
Fairy dust!
Magic dust!
It fell like little stars onto Wendy, John and Michael.
Think of something lovely, said Peter.
Something that makes you happy.
Christmas.
Sweets.
Snow.
And suddenly: up!
They floated off the ground!
They were flying!
Wheee!
They flew out of the window, over the roofs of London, past the big clock called Big Ben.
Bong, bong!
Second star to the right, and straight on till morning!
They arrived in Never Land.
An island full of mountains, waterfalls, forests and beaches.
Mermaids lived there, lying on the rocks.
Native children and animals lived there.
And the Lost Boys lived there, who dressed up as little bears and foxes and bunnies.
They lived in a secret house under a tree.
But in the bay lay a big pirate ship.
With black sails and a flag with a skull.
And on that ship lived the wicked Captain Hook.
Captain Hook had a red coat, a big hat with a feather and a long, curly black moustache.
And instead of his left hand he had an iron hook.
Because long ago, in a fight, Peter Pan had fed his hand to a crocodile.
The crocodile thought Captain Hook was so tasty that it followed him everywhere.
It wanted to eat the rest of him too!
Captain Hook was super scared of that crocodile.
Really super scared!
And do you know what was so funny?
The crocodile had also swallowed an alarm clock.
And that clock was still in its tummy.
So wherever the crocodile swam, you heard: Tick-tock.
Tick-tock.
Tick-tock.
When Captain Hook heard that, he turned completely pale.
He shook from his hat to his boots.
Smee!
Smee!
Help!
It's the crocodile!
And then he jumped into the arms of his chubby pirate helper, Smee.
Hee hee hee!
Wendy and the boys had wonderful adventures.
They swam with the mermaids.
They danced around the campfire.
They flew through the sky with Peter.
But Captain Hook caught Wendy and the Lost Boys.
He put them on his ship.
They had to walk the plank, above the water.
And in the water swam the crocodile.
Tick-tock, tick-tock.
But here came Peter Pan, flying in!
Whoosh!
I'm here!
he shouted.
Peter and Captain Hook fought with their swords.
Cling, clang, cling!
Peter flew around his head.
Peekaboo, Hook, here I am!
He was much too fast.
And suddenly: splash!
Captain Hook fell into the water.
And who was waiting there with its mouth open?
Tick-tock, tick-tock, the crocodile!
Help, help!
Captain Hook swam away as fast as he could, with the crocodile right behind him.
Snap, snap, snap!
Hee hee hee!
Everyone laughed.
Tinker Bell sprinkled fairy dust over the whole pirate ship.
Ping!
And the ship flew through the sky, with golden sails, back to London.
Wendy, John and Michael landed safely in their beds.
And Peter Pan waved and flew back to Never Land.
Bye!
And if you listen carefully at night, maybe you'll hear Tinker Bell's ping-ping at your window.
